title: Regex Tester
description: Regex Tester helps people test regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text and review the result before using it in another system.
intro: Regex Tester is for a concrete handoff: take regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text from a real task, produce the form the next editor, API, document, or workflow expects, and keep enough context to verify what changed.
audience: Developers, data analysts, QA engineers, and technical support teams
input: A pattern, flags, and sample text containing both expected matches and deliberate non-matches for Regex Tester.
outcome: A regex tester result that preserves the intended meaning and is ready to test in its destination.
review: Check positive and negative samples, groups, greediness, boundaries, Unicode, multiline behavior, and compatibility with the destination regex engine.
bestFor: Small and medium regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text samples used for debugging, documentation, migration preparation, review, and reproducible tests.
steps: Paste a representative pattern and test sample from the task you are working on.
Run Regex Tester and compare the first meaningful change with the source.
Inspect matches, groups, non-matches, and edge cases.
Copy or download the result, then validate it in the editor, runtime, API, form, or publishing system where it will be used.
useCases: Regex Tester for a real development or integration task rather than a synthetic keyword example.
Preparing Regex Tester input and output for a bug report, documentation page, test fixture, or technical handoff.
Using Regex Tester against failures and edge cases before adding the pattern to application code.
Regex Tester helps catch structural or meaning-changing mistakes before the output reaches another system.

examples.title: Regex Tester with a representative sample
examples.description: This Regex Tester example uses regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text that resembles a small production fixture, so the main change can be checked line by line.

examples.title: Regex Tester edge-case review
examples.description: The second Regex Tester pass focuses on the part most likely to fail: boundaries and non-matches.
examples.input:
/\b[A-Z]{2}-\d{4}\b/g
Tickets: AB-1042, invalid A-22, CD-8801

Review case: preserve empty, repeated, or non-ASCII values where applicable.
examples.output:
Matches (2)
AB-1042
CD-8801

Review note: confirm this result in the destination workflow.

tips: Keep the original Regex Tester input beside the result until the destination check passes.
Use realistic regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text instead of a one-word sample when validating Regex Tester.
Do not assume the visual cleanup from Regex Tester proves that regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text is valid.
Run the normal project, API, schema, browser, or editorial validation after using Regex Tester.

faq.question: Who uses Regex Tester?
faq.answer: Developers, data analysts, QA engineers, and technical support teams use Regex Tester when they need to test regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text before continuing work in another editor, system, or document.

faq.question: What should I paste into Regex Tester?
faq.answer: Paste a focused but representative sample of regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text into Regex Tester. Include the nesting, punctuation, characters, or edge cases that affect the real task.

faq.question: What does Regex Tester change?
faq.answer: Regex Tester changes the representation needed for this task. Compare the output with the source to confirm that values and intended meaning remain correct.

faq.question: What should I check after using Regex Tester?
faq.answer: After Regex Tester, review matches, non-matches, groups, flags, greediness, boundaries, and the regex flavor used by the destination runtime.

faq.question: Can I use the Regex Tester output in production?
faq.answer: Use the Regex Tester result as reviewed working output, then run the destination system's normal validation, tests, schema checks, or editorial review before production use.

faq.question: Does Regex Tester store my input?
faq.answer: Regex Tester has no account or saved-history feature. Even so, remove passwords, private keys, session cookies, personal data, and production secrets before using any online tool.

keywords: test regular-expression patterns, flags, groups, and representative test text
commonMistakes: Running Regex Tester with a sample that does not represent the real input.
Using the Regex Tester result without comparing it with the original source.
Skipping validation in the editor, runtime, API, or document that receives the output.
